clips.text_zh: WHERE IS THE MONEY GOING? GOLD crashing, SILVER crashing, STOCKS crashing, BITCOIN crashing. The fuck is going on!!! 😱 靠，又係全部一齊跌。
clips.text_en_b1: Where is the money going? Gold is crashing. Silver is crashing. Stocks are crashing. Bitcoin is crashing. The fuck is going on?! I checked the obvious charts and nothing makes sense. This is the kind of market panic that turns a normal CFD loss into a very expensive tuition.
clips.text_en_b2: Where is all the money going? Gold is crashing, silver is crashing, stocks are crashing, and Bitcoin is crashing at the same time. What the hell is going on?! I checked the obvious charts, but nothing makes any sense. Markets usually correct themselves, although a synchronized plunge this broad looks more like panic than a routine pullback. That is how a normal CFD loss can quickly become a very expensive tuition.
clips.text_en_c1: Where on earth is the money going? Gold is crashing, silver is crashing, stocks are crashing, and Bitcoin is crashing all at once. What the fuck is happening here? I stared at every obvious chart, and nothing on any of them makes sense. This is precisely the sort of market panic in which an ordinary CFD loss balloons into a very expensive tuition bill. When everything falls together, correlations break down, liquidity evaporates, and the sensible thing to do is not to keep staring at the screen.
clips.text_en_c2: Where is all the money going? Gold is crashing, silver is crashing, equities are crashing, and Bitcoin is sliding just as hard. What the hell is happening? I checked the most obvious charts, yet none of the usual explanations makes sense; everything appears to be liquidating in unison. This is precisely the sort of indiscriminate market panic that converts an ordinary CFD loss into an exceptionally expensive tuition bill. The crucial point, however, is that surviving such turbulence requires discipline rather than impulsive trades.
clips.source_hint: An anon watches gold, silver, stocks, and Bitcoin fall together.

clips.text_zh: Elon Musk is 589 posting. You know what this means, #XRPArmy. Prepare accordingly. 又出post啦。膠膠吶，準備定未？
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk is 589, posting. You know what this means, #XRPArmy. Prepare accordingly. His posts can move a token quickly, but chasing the first candle is how CFD traders turn tuition into tuition. Watch the reaction, do not blindly buy the mention.
clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk is 589-posting again. You know what that means, #XRPArmy: prepare accordingly. His announcements can send a token flying in minutes, but chasing the first candle is how CFD traders turn one tuition payment into two. Although the mention may create genuine momentum, it does not guarantee a lasting move. Watch how the market reacts, let the initial frenzy settle, and do not blindly buy the mention.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk is on a 589 posting spree, and everyone in the #XRPArmy already knows what that implies: prepare accordingly. His posts have historically been enough to move a token within minutes, but chasing that first candle is exactly how CFD traders turn one tuition payment into two. The rational play is to watch how the market reacts, to let the initial spike settle, and only then decide whether the mention was signal or noise. Do not blindly buy the mention.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk is at it again with post number 589. You know perfectly well what this implies, #XRPArmy: prepare accordingly. His announcements have repeatedly demonstrated an astonishing ability to move a token within minutes, but chasing the first green candle is precisely how CFD traders turn tuition into a recurring expense. The sensible approach is to watch the reaction, allow the initial volatility to settle, and assess whether the mention has translated into sustained demand. Never confuse a headline with a trading strategy.
clips.source_hint: A trader reacts to Elon Musk's social-media post about 589.

clips.text_zh: OMG, Elon just announced that the singularity has started. Did you think this moment would ever happen? 靠AI續命既年代真係嚟啦。
clips.text_en_b1: OMG, Elon just announced that the singularity has started. Did you think this moment would ever happen? AI may improve fast, but engineers will still need to check the load path, understand the design, and explain decisions on site. Automation does not remove engineering judgment. It changes the tools we use.
clips.text_en_b2: OMG, Elon has just announced that the singularity has started. Did you ever think this moment would actually arrive? AI is certainly improving at an extraordinary pace, but engineers will still have to check load paths, understand the underlying design, and explain critical decisions on site. Although automation may perform repetitive work far more efficiently, it does not eliminate engineering judgment. Instead, it changes the tools we use and the way we apply that judgment.
clips.text_en_c1: OMG, Elon has just announced that the singularity has officially begun. Did you ever actually believe this moment would arrive? Whatever the timeline, AI may well improve at a blistering pace; however, engineers will still have to inspect the load path, grasp the underlying design, and account for their decisions on site when something fails. Automation does not abolish engineering judgment. It simply replaces the tools we reach for, and it relocates where responsibility sits.
clips.text_en_c2: OMG, Elon has just announced that the singularity has begun. Did you ever imagine this moment would actually arrive? AI may be advancing at a breathtaking pace, but the engineers who deploy it will still have to verify load paths, understand the underlying design, and explain consequential decisions on site when circumstances change. Automation does not abolish engineering judgment; it reshapes the tools we use and the standards we apply to them. We should remain cautiously optimistic, since technological breakthroughs rarely eliminate practical responsibility overnight.
clips.source_hint: An anon reacts to Elon Musk's announcement about the technological singularity.

clips.text_zh: Elon Musk announced we are officially in the singularity. Things to look forward to: immortality, UBI, flying cars, immersive video games. Everything will be free. Money will be meaningless. Life will be a permanent vacation. 然後我個prop firm就更加唔使愁啦？
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk announced we are officially in the singularity. Things to look forward to include immortality, UBI, flying cars, and immersive video games. All of it will be free. Money will be meaningless. Life will be a permanent vacation for all of us. Our only challenge will be sorting through all the options.
clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk has announced that we are officially living in the singularity. Apparently, there is plenty to look forward to: immortality, universal basic income, flying cars, and immersive video games. Everything is going to be free, money will become meaningless, and life for all of us will resemble a permanent vacation. Although our main problem may no longer be paying the bills, we will still have to choose between all these options.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has announced that we are officially living in the singularity, so here is what there is to look forward to: immortality, universal basic income, flying cars, and immersive video games. All of it will presumably be free. Money will become meaningless, and life will amount to a permanent vacation for every one of us. The only real difficulty left will be triaging an overwhelming surplus of options, and deciding which of them is actually worth your time.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk has announced that we are officially living in the singularity. The anticipated delights include immortality, universal basic income, flying cars, and immersive video games, with everything supposedly becoming free. Money would become meaningless, while life degenerates into an endless vacation for everybody. Our sole difficulty would then be deciding which experience to choose from an overwhelming catalogue of alternatives. The irony is obvious: if every human need were effortlessly satisfied, nobody would need the prop firm I am presently trying to sustain.
clips.source_hint: A satirical post imagines a post-singularity world with free money and flying cars.

clips.text_zh: I switched over to bodybuilding. At home: floor press with 36 kg kettlebells, at least 15 reps total each day, followed by band pull-aparts. Every 2 days at the gym: deadlift and dumbbell bench, one set of 5 or more reps. Deadlift 180 kg x 5 at 73 kg bodyweight. 靠，呢個負荷先似男人。
clips.text_en_b1: I switched over to bodybuilding. At home, I floor press with 36 kg kettlebells for at least 15 reps each day, followed by band pull-aparts. Every two days at the gym, I deadlift and dumbbell bench for one set of five or more reps. My deadlift is 180 kg for five reps at 73 kg bodyweight.
clips.text_en_b2: I switched over to bodybuilding, and the results are becoming noticeably more respectable. At home, I floor-press with 36-kilogram kettlebells, completing at least 15 repetitions in total each day, followed by band pull-aparts. Every two days at the gym, I deadlift and dumbbell-bench for one set of five or more repetitions. The main achievement is a deadlift of 180 kilograms for five reps at 73 kilograms of bodyweight.
clips.text_en_c1: I switched over to bodybuilding, and the routine is simple enough to keep. At home, I floor press with 36 kg kettlebells, logging at least 15 reps in total each day, followed by band pull-aparts. Every second day at the gym, I deadlift and dumbbell bench for one set of five reps or more. My deadlift currently stands at 180 kg for five reps, achieved at a bodyweight of 73 kg, which is the only figure on this list I am actually proud of.
clips.text_en_c2: I switched over to bodybuilding, and the routine is now deliberately demanding. At home, I floor-press with 36-kilogram kettlebells for at least 15 repetitions every day, immediately followed by band pull-aparts. Every second day in the gym, I deadlift and dumbbell-bench, completing one set of five or more repetitions. My heaviest deadlift stands at 180 kilograms for five reps, achieved at a bodyweight of only 73 kilograms. It is a considerable load, though I would rather celebrate steady progress than make any reckless claims about masculinity.
clips.source_hint: The OP describes a bodybuilding program and a 180 kg deadlift.

clips.text_zh: Sonic Racing CrossWorlds: McLaren Festival Day 4. Another day, another Festival grind. Take a break from the GTA VI slop and play a game that makes your blood boil. Also, post your lobbies. 又係每日 grind。
clips.text_en_b1: Sonic Racing CrossWorlds: McLaren Festival, Day 4. Another day and another Festival grind. Take a break from the GTA VI slop and play a game that makes your blood boil. Also, post your lobbies so other players can join. Sometimes the best way to stop thinking about losing trades is to race.
clips.text_en_b2: Sonic Racing CrossWorlds: McLaren Festival, Day 4. It is another day and another Festival grind, but at least it gives you a break from the bloated nonsense surrounding GTA VI. Play a game that makes your blood boil, then post your lobbies so other players can join. Although the repetitive grind can become frustrating, racing is usually more satisfying than staring at losing trades. Sometimes the fastest way to stop thinking about the market is to race.
clips.text_en_c1: Sonic Racing CrossWorlds: McLaren Festival, Day 4. Another day, another Festival grind, and the routine wears no less repetitive than it did yesterday. Take a break from the GTA VI slop and play something that genuinely makes your blood boil. If you do, post your lobbies afterwards so that other players can join in and you are not racing alone. Sometimes the most effective cure for brooding over losing trades is simply to floor it and forget the charts.
clips.text_en_c2: Sonic Racing CrossWorlds: McLaren Festival, Day 4, brings another instalment of that familiar Festival grind. Take a break from the insipid GTA VI sludge and play a game that genuinely gets your blood racing rather than merely boiling with frustration. The Festival provides a welcome change of pace, provided you can tolerate the relentless repetition. Do post your lobbies as well, so other players know where to join and nobody has to grind alone. Sometimes the most effective remedy for dwelling on losing trades is simply to race.
clips.source_hint: A gaming thread promotes the fourth day of the McLaren Festival and asks for lobbies.

clips.text_en_c1: Ranma 1/2 storytime. I am going to run the manga alongside the new anime season, which means anons can compare and contrast, or else experience the story in a completely different medium at the same time. Today we are covering chapters 100 to 102. This thread is a discussion space for sharing reactions, arguments about the adaptations, and how far along each of you happens to be in the reading.
clips.text_en_c2: Ranma 1/2 storytime. I am going to work through the manga alongside the new anime season, giving us two complementary ways to engage with the same story and an opportunity to compare their respective treatments. Some anons may follow the original material, while others will experience these developments for the first time through the animated adaptation; either way, the overlap should fuel interesting discussion. clips.source_hint: The OP starts a Ranma 1/2 manga storytime for chapters 100 through 102.
